title: Vintage Gibson ES-125 Value Guide: Annual Price Ranges
description: Vintage Gibson ES-125 values from 1941 to 1970, with annual price references, condition notes, variant context and photographs from my own guitar archive.
alt: Sunburst 1954 ES-125 with one black pickup, two controls and a trapeze tailpiece

faqs.q: How Much Is A 1950s Gibson ES-125 Worth?
faqs.a: A full-depth, full-size, single-pickup sunburst ES-125 from 1950 to 1959 has a guide range of $2,500 to $3,250 in excellent condition with original parts and the original case. These values were reviewed in October 2026. Replaced parts or repairs need a separate appraisal.

faqs.q: Does The Table Include ES-125TDC Values?
faqs.a: No. The annual table covers the full-depth, full-size, single-pickup ES-125. A TDC has a thin body, a cutaway and two pickups. I haven't assigned it the standard model's range or invented a fixed premium.

faqs.q: Why Are There No Rows From 1943 Through 1945?
faqs.a: The early run covers 1941 and 1942, with postwar production restarting in 1946. A guitar described differently needs its model and date established before using the table.

faqs.q: Is An ES-125 A Semi-Hollow Guitar?
faqs.a: The ES-125 is a hollow archtop rather than a center-block design like the ES-335. Body depth and the presence of a cutaway identify different ES-125 variants, but they don't by themselves add a center block.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Reduce It To A Modified Guitar?
faqs.a: Under this site's grading approach, a quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar and removes museum-quality status. A neck repair, reshaping or changed pickup is a separate issue.

faqs.q: Can I Use A Sold Listing Price Without Checking The Details?
faqs.a: No. A completed-price category can include the wrong variant, a repaired guitar or even a different model. I check the listing's year, configuration and disclosed work before using it as a comparison.
